 Vivo V80, S2 and Y11 5G prices hiked in India by up to Rs 5,000
 By Saloni Tandon - Published On: 16 November 2026 | 12:16 IST Highlights Vivo V80 and S2 prices have reportedly increased by Rs 5,000 across all variants. 
 The Vivo Y11 5G is said to have become costlier by Rs 3,000. 
 The new prices haven’t appeared on Vivo’s official website yet, and the company hasn’t issued a statement. 
 If you thought the worst was behind us in terms of the recent smartphone price hikes, think again. Vivo has reportedly increased the prices of three smartphones in India, including the newly launched Vivo V80. According to tipster Gadgetsdata , the Vivo V80 and Vivo S2 will become costlier by Rs 5,000 and the Y11 5G will get a Rs 3,000 hike across all variants. The updated prices are yet to appear on Vivo’s official website, and the company hasn’t officially announced the changes, though the tipster said the changes were due to be in place from November 
 Vivo V80, S2, Y11 5G new prices 
 The Vivo V80 now reportedly starts at Rs 67,999 for the 8GB + 128GB variant, up from Rs 62,999. The 8GB + 256GB and 8GB + 512GB configurations now cost Rs 74,999 and Rs 84,999, respectively, as per the new report. 
 The Vivo S2’s 8GB + 128GB variant will now allegedly cost Rs 47,999, while the 8GB + 256GB model will be priced at Rs 53,999. Both have received a Rs 5,000 increase. 
 The Vivo Y11 5G has received a Rs 3,000 hike. Its 4GB + 64GB variant is said to cost Rs 21,999, while the 4GB + 128GB version is priced at Rs 25,499. This takes the starting price of a 4GB RAM 5G smartphone with 64GB storage beyond Rs 20,000.

 Should you buy the phones? 
 The Vivo V80 faces competition from the OPPO Reno 16 and Xiaomi 17T . The Reno 16 starts at Rs 65,999 for 8GB + 128GB and offers the same Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 chipset, along with a 50MP triple rear camera setup that includes a telephoto lens. The Xiaomi 17T, meanwhile, starts at Rs 69,999 for 12GB + 256GB and brings a more powerful Dimensity 8500 Ultra chipset, a Leica-tuned 50MP main camera and a 50MP 5x periscope telephoto camera. Both are more compelling on paper at their respective starting prices. The V80’s 7,200mAh battery, 144Hz display and Zeiss camera tuning are advantages, but its 8GB + 128GB base configuration is difficult to justify at Rs 67,999. 
 The Vivo S2 is in an equally difficult position. At Rs 47,999, it competes directly with the Motorola Edge 70 Pro+, which offers a Dimensity 8500 Extreme chipset, 12GB RAM, 256GB storage, a 144Hz 1.5K display and a 50MP periscope camera with 3.5x optical zoom. The S2’s 7,050mAh battery is larger, but its older Dimensity 7360 Turbo chipset and slower 44W charging make the Motorola a better overall purchase. 
 The Rs 3,000 hike makes the Y11 5G particularly difficult to recommend. At Rs 21,999 for the 4GB+64GB variant, it’s in the same range as the POCO M8x and Redmi 17C 5G , with the former starting at Rs 18,999 (4GB + 128GB) and Rs 21,999 (4GB + 128GB). The POCO is the stronger option for battery life and charging, with a 7,900mAh battery and 45W charging, while the Redmi offers a more balanced package with a 50MP primary camera and 33W charging. The Y11 5G does have a 6,500mAh battery, but its 13MP rear camera, 15W charging and lower base storage make the premium difficult to justify.
